title: GAIL opposes IGX platform for LNG terminal capacity booking
summary: India's top gas marketer GAIL opposes a new platform for booking LNG terminal capacity. GAIL states this platform will add costs for consumers without significant value. The company believes existing frameworks do not require a separate booking platform. High global LNG prices already pressure downstream natural gas consumers. Much of India's LNG regasification capacity remains underutilised currently.

title: Shifting Gears: PSBs borrow more to cater to credit demand as deposits lag
summary: Public sector banks are borrowing more to fund lending expansion. Deposits are not keeping pace with credit growth for these banks. Private banks show stronger deposit growth and are gaining market share. This trend raises concerns about funding sustainability for state-owned lenders. Abundant system liquidity currently cushions the impact of these shifts.

title: Fire insurance premiums fall 28% in Q1 amid deep discounting
summary: Fire insurance premiums dropped significantly in the first four months of the financial year. Aggressive discounting on large industrial risks pressured insurers competing for corporate accounts. The regulator received complaints of steep discounts, raising financial health concerns. Major insurers like New India Assurance and ICICI Lombard saw premium reductions. Pricing for industrial fire risks must now follow sound actuarial principles.

title: Tata Power loses challenge to $490 million arbitration award
summary: Tata Power's challenge to a $490 million arbitration award was rejected by Singapore's court.  The court upheld damages awarded to Kleros Capital Partners regarding a Russian coal asset bid.  Disagreements over leadership and ownership soured the partnership in 2015.  Kleros alleged Tata Power misused confidential information and acted in bad faith.  The company must now pay Kleros' legal costs, which are yet to be determined.

title: Adani Energy wins Rs 4,700 crore Maharashtra transmission project; shares rise

AESL's transmission order book now stands at Rs 85,000 crore.
